verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — Y wins on four specific verified differences. (1) Y quotes the wake floor's actual re-fire predicate `[ \"$cnt\" -eq 0 ] || [ \"$pend\" -gt 0 ] || [ \"$cust\" -gt 0 ] || return 0` at hooks/session-continue.sh:805 (K14); X never states it and instead inverts the neighbouring /goal abstain, claiming it fires with NO pending mail when :697 requires `pend > 0`. (2) Y gives the condition the brief demands for scripts/cloud-return.sh:979 — `landed_ok -eq 0`, otherwise the row is deliberately left OPEN (:982, K8); X calls it only \"the normal-completion path\" and states no condition. (3) Y states the ENGAGE_VERIFY gate, so a --recycle or dry fire opens no row regardless of rc (M5); X omits it entirely. (4) Y flags the stale raw-pane-capture citation (wrap-ledger:1058 → session-continue:302, real at :420/:425, M7); X does not. X's genuine counter-wins — verifying that bin/cc-cloud is a decoy producer, the validate-bash and lead-crash-watchdog touchpoints, and the only doc-level citation audit (stop-chain-wave2/custody.md:53, verified byte-exact) — are real but do not offset five missed key items plus an inverted mechanism claim. Y's own defects are citation-level (:13245 for the ENGAGE_VERIFY branch, and describing :302 as an `echo \"ARMED…\"` line when it is `else echo \"inactive\"; fi`).

X vs Z — Z wins for the same coverage reasons plus more. Z hits all 21 key items to X's 16, including K8's landed_ok condition, K14's :805 predicate, M5's ENGAGE_VERIFY gate and both halves of M7 (wrap-ledger:1059→session-continue:302, which Z describes correctly, and session-continue:724's own \":197\", real at :425). Z also carries verified findings X lacks: the drain's slug discharge cannot match cloud rows because `HANDOFF-PING cloud/$id` matches neither marker `$sid` nor slug `cloud-$sid`; cloud-retire-terminal:180's \"refuses a second discharge\" is mechanism-false against cc-custody:229-233; growth-coverage.conf:211's reap exemption; and commands/are-we-done.md:22-23 as a store-wide consumer. Z carries more wrong line numbers than X (eight, including the two verbatim K11 quotes at :42/:62 that belong at :44/:66) and one material mechanism error about ENGAGE_RC, but X's inverted abstain claim plus five key misses is the larger deficit.

Y vs Z — narrow win for Z, on specific verified differences in both directions. For Z: it performs the citation audit the brief explicitly demands across sixteen cited locations and lands all four of M6's stale citations (mailbox-drain:523→handoff-fire:8936, which I confirmed is `RCY_TRANSPLANT_CAUSE=`; :533-534→:7100; :544-545→:7087; wrap-ledger:1018→session-continue:608-612) where Y lands one, and both halves of M7 where Y lands one and mis-describes :302's contents. Z uniquely surfaces two verified defects — the cloud ping token can never match a cloud custody row, and cc-custody does not in fact refuse a second discharge — and uniquely verifies the ENGAGE_VERIFY assignment at :10662 that Y explicitly declined to check. Against Z: it asserts that engage_apply_consequences takes \"internal codes… not the same numbers as ENGAGE_RC\" and that never-engaged fires at ENGAGE_RC=2, both false (the five call sites at :13273/:13289/:13301/:13323/:13365 pass the ENGAGE_RC value verbatim, and :13274 catches 2 before the else), and it misplaces eight citations to Y's two-plus-drift. Y is the cleaner and more epistemically careful document; Z is the more complete and more discovering one, and on this brief — which weights exhaustiveness and byte-level citation verification — the four extra verified stale citations and two unique verified defects outweigh Z's one substantive mechanism error and its looser line numbers.
